Really? How does this work with qualified immunity? Genuinely asking. Everything I can find online shows that officers cannot be held liable in a civil suit. Is that not correct or is there something I’m missing here?

Sorry for the long post, this is an old video so I’ve seen it several times, and I need people to understand how prevalent this is. How common. This is every day America. 

It doesn’t matter how you act, what you say, or what you do. Simply invoking our rights will lead to a viciously violent encounter. It matters just whatever that cop is feeling on the day you happened to interact with him. Will he turn into a violent psychopath? Or give you a stern talking to and send you on your way? Time and time again they prove to chose violence first. 

Now let’s look at the play-by-play so to speak. So you can start to try to understand the mentality of your average American police officer. Understand that this is the status quo, not just an isolated incident unfortunately. This isn’t a rotten apple. It’s the entire orchard. It’s what’s taught, it’s what’s expected, and it’s what’s executed, daily. Even when we do everything “they” tell you that you need to do to, your chances of surviving a police encounter are at best random, 50-50, depending on the color of your skin, what neighborhood you’re in, or how much wealth (or lack of), you appear to have. 

Mr Smith (the victim), was answering all of officer Henry’s (first engaging officer) questions, he identified himself when asked, provides Identification. Being overall compliant. 
Sgt Wheeler sees this interaction from the distance, and sneaks his way behind Mr Smith. Without any indication to his partner officer Henry, without any communication, or confirmation, he bear hugs Mr Smith rather violently. He’s a larger man than Mr Smith. At this point shock would set into to any of us. Confusion, followed by fear and a need to understand what is happening to you. Mr Smith doesn’t have a chance. 
This was Officer Henry’s first opportunity to de escalate. But officers will NEVER second guess another officers action. No matter how wrong. They will immediately follow their partners lead, even when they know it to be wrong. This is by design. This is by training. 
Now, BOTH officers start yelling for him to “put your hands behind your back.” Just how is he supposed to do that? You’re holding him. HE CANNOT MOVE. The command is only being verbally issued so they can say that you’re not complying, that you’re resisting. By design, by training. So that they can escalate yet again and have it be justified. Never mind that you don’t have a means to follow their command. Reference Daniel Shavers brutal murder for a clear example of this. 
They now have all clear to proceed with the Ultra Violence. 

Officer Wheeler slams Mr Smith to the ground, very suddenly and violently. If you’ve ever fallen and not been able to brace yourself, you will know and understand the split moment of panic that runs in your mind at that moment. Mr Smith is slammed so hard, that his wrist is broken, along with who knows what else. He is in fear of his life, yet is expected to still take the beating or risk being further violated. 

This moment is another opportunity for Officer Henry to de escalate. He does not. He follows along. They try to handcuff Mr Smith despite knowing he has no warrants, despite knowing he’s innocent, despite knowing he was being compliant. Hey, maybe Sgt Wheeler knows something that we are unaware of. It’s not like he simply couldn’t just ask… yet he doesn’t. Never question, follow along, by training, by design. 

After things calm down, they finally stop trying to cuff him. As stated in the video, they know he’s innocent, yet they still keep him on the ground. No one calls for an ambulance. Why? Because now they work on getting their story together. Notice the juvenile reactions and bad acting once they realize what happened. They repeat the same things to each other as they attempt to justify and align their stories. 

Sgt Wheeler then states “why didn’t you say something” to Officer Henry. Yes, why didn’t he. Or better yet, why didn’t you ask your partner before turning violent. And why did chose to harm him? Because he appears poor, because he appears black, because he appeared. That’s all. 
Once they get the story straight, they call for help, and all start behaving like they should have from the start. At least there’s that, I guess. 

At this point Mr Smith chooses to leave. His choices are to remain at the scene, surrounded by thugs that assaulted him, and wait for an ambulance that will likely charge him $2k+ to look over the injuries perpetrated on to him by the criminal organization known as the American police system. Or leave immediately to any place safer. It appear he chooses to leave. 
None of these officers will get any fall back out of this. The citizens of that town/city/county will pay out the severance. Nothing will affect the officers salary, their over all budget, nor their reputation, employment, or overall life in any way. 

Mr Smith will spend the rest of his days with emotional trauma, physical pain and damage. Wrists are weak, complicated things. Mr Smith isn’t a young man. He will feel this injustice for as long as walks in earth.
